data.heading: Where it started
data.description: A governance blind spot opening up as AI adoption accelerated across the enterprise, ahead of any central system for tracking external AI vendors.

blocks.title: Business problem
blocks.body: Teams across the business adopted third-party AI tools on their own, spanning generative image and audio tools, AI coding assistants, and other categories. Leadership could answer none of the basic governance questions: which vendors are in use, by whom, and what data they access.

blocks.title: Lack of decision framework
blocks.body: Each review ran manually and took two to three weeks, so the backlog grew faster than the team could clear it. Approvals, rejections, and remediations were handled case by case, the audit trail lived in email, and a change in a vendor's risk profile, a breach or a contract deviation, surfaced only after the fact.

blocks.title: Agivant's role
blocks.body: Architecture, agent engineering, workflow design, and production rollout across detection, assessment, decisioning, and remediation

data.heading: What Agivant built
data.description: Forward Deployed Engineers embedded with the vendor strategy and operations function through problem discovery, architecture, workflow design, and production rollout. Risk signals arrive continuously, an LLM drafts the assessment, an analyst rules on it through the dashboard, and the workflow engine executes the approved action. Value in days and weeks.

blocks.title: Automated risk detection
blocks.body: Continuously monitors vendor risk signals pulled from multiple data sources, raising an alert as each one appears.

blocks.title: AI-powered assessment
blocks.body: An LLM scores severity, proposes a remediation path, and recommends an owner, turning a raw alert into an actionable recommendation.

blocks.title: Human-in-the-loop decisions
blocks.body: Analysts review every AI-generated recommendation through an interactive dashboard and can approve it, reject it, or send it back for replanning.

blocks.title: Iterative replan loop
blocks.body: On a replan request the AI agent revises its recommendation and its reasoning, for as many rounds as the analyst needs.

blocks.title: Automated remediation orchestration
blocks.body: Once a decision is approved, the workflow engine executes the remediation action automatically.

blocks.title: Audit and compliance logging
blocks.body: Every decision, human and AI, is captured in a structured log built to support regulatory and compliance reporting.

blocks.title: Real-time notifications
blocks.body: Risk owners and stakeholders are alerted the moment a decision or an action is needed.

blocks.title: Error handling and escalation
blocks.body: Failed actions are caught, logged, and escalated along a defined path, so nothing disappears silently.

rows.label: Architecture
rows.value: Three layers, data, orchestration, and presentation, each able to evolve independently

rows.label: Workflow engine
rows.value: n8n, orchestrating risk assessment, decision routing, and remediation execution

rows.label: Dashboard
rows.value: Next.js, the interactive human-in-the-loop interface for risk analysts

rows.label: AI risk scanning
rows.value: PromptArmor, for third-party AI security scanning and vulnerability detection

rows.label: Data store
rows.value: Enterprise data warehouse tables plus a configuration sheet, holding alert logs, decision logs, and error tracking

rows.label: Production workflows
rows.value: Orchestrator as the HITL decision router, executor as the remediation engine

rows.label: Notifications
rows.value: Chat API integration, alerting risk owners in real time

rows.label: Security
rows.value: JWT (HS256) signed webhooks, a secure reverse proxy for external API calls, keychain-managed secrets

rows.label: Governance controls
rows.value: Analyst approval required on every action before it executes

blocks.title: Before
blocks.body: A manual, ad hoc review process tracked in email, with each function keeping its own separate view of vendor risk.

blocks.title: After
blocks.body: An agent layer feeding AI-drafted assessments into the analyst dashboard, approved decisions executing and logging automatically, and one shared governance record across security, legal, procurement, and engineering.

data.heading: Proof in production
data.description: An alert reaches an analyst carrying vendor, severity, priority, risk category, a plain-language summary, the AI confidence score, a remediation path, an owner, an effort estimate, and an SLA. The analyst approves, rejects, or requests a replan, and the agent returns a revised plan with its reasoning. Approved decisions route to the executor, which runs the action, logs it, and notifies stakeholders.

blocks.heading: Measured results
blocks.description: The same team of analysts, using the same judgment they always brought to vendor risk, now covers 10x the ground because the AI does the first-pass analysis and the workflow engine handles execution.

blocks.title: Reusable asset
blocks.body: A reusable HITL pattern, AI proposes, human decides, system executes, that extends to any governance domain needing AI-assisted recommendations with human accountability, and lays the foundation for an AI Consumption Control Tower across all external AI usage. Every build amplifies the next.

blocks.title: Challenges overcome
blocks.body: Keeping a human ruling on every decision while clearing the bottleneck the manual process had created. The AI first pass had to arrive complete enough for an analyst to act in minutes, and the replan loop covers the cases that need a second look before anything executes.
